answer: Each agent receives a nontransferable credential only after completing a randomly assigned task whose result is checked against a hidden test; credentials expire and must be renewed with a different task. Payments require a credential, and one credential can authorize only one active account, so copying identities does not multiply earning capacity. An attacker must repeatedly spend compute and time producing independently verified work for every additional account. A velvet interface, a relic record, or a willow-themed name cannot substitute for that costly proof.
